notes.Giannis Antetokounmpo: Bam Adebayo sat the second half Monday with right hip tightness and Giannis slid to center; Adebayo is probable tonight and Miami does not expect the hip to linger. Giannis has played 29 to 31 minutes in each of his last three games, and Miami is a 12.5-point favorite in his first game against Milwaukee, so a lopsided game could cap his minutes again.
notes.Cade Cunningham: Detroit is on the second night of a back-to-back after Tuesday's comeback win in San Antonio, where he played 38 minutes. Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson, Taurean Prince and Ronald Holland II were all out Tuesday, and Detroit has not posted tonight's injury report yet.
notes.Jalen Johnson: CJ McCollum (calf) and Kingston Flemings (lumbar strain) are both out, so Atlanta's ball handling falls to him, Dyson Daniels and RayJ Dennis. Jock Landale is also out, which keeps Johnson playing big minutes; he played 40 and 35 in his last two games.
notes.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, so the offense runs through him. Atlanta is missing six players, including CJ McCollum and its backup big men, which favors a comfortable Thunder night; his minutes dropped to 30 Sunday after 39 the game before.
notes.Cameron Boozer: Memphis is short again: Ty Jerome (right hip) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are out, and GG Jackson had foot surgery Tuesday and will miss about three months. Boozer took on more of the scoring with Jerome out Monday, and his minutes were 29 in each of his last two games.
notes.Taylor Hendricks: Isaiah Stewart (illness) is out again and GG Jackson is out for months after foot surgery, so Memphis has fewer frontcourt options behind Zach Edey. He played 19 minutes Monday with Edey back, after 29 on 11/14 when Edey sat.
notes.Jerami Grant: He has settled into a steady bench role, playing 23 to 26 minutes in his last two games. Ty Jerome, Isaiah Stewart, GG Jackson and Scotty Pippen Jr. are all out, so Memphis has few other scorers to take his minutes.
notes.Corey Kispert: CJ McCollum (calf) and Kingston Flemings (back) are out, which opens wing and guard minutes in Atlanta. He played 16 minutes off the bench Sunday, and the wing minutes have been rotating among him, Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins.
notes.Anfernee Simons: Jaylen Brown is out with a left hamstring strain he felt late Monday, which opens shots and minutes on the wing. Simons played 26 minutes off the bench Monday after foul trouble held him to 15 on Sunday.
notes.Jaylen Wells: He has started each of Memphis's last three games at 25 to 27 minutes. Ty Jerome and Isaiah Stewart are out again and GG Jackson is out for months, so his role stays steady.
notes.Jordan Poole: Trey Murphy III (knee, sixth straight absence), Dejounte Murray (ankle) and Bennedict Mathurin are all out, and Poole's bench minutes have climbed from 21 and 24 to 31 on Monday. Detroit is on the second night of a back-to-back.
notes.L.J. Cryer: Stephen Curry (oblique tear) and Brandon Williams (hamstring) are out, which opens guard minutes in Golden State. Draymond Green (elbow) and Al Horford (back) are questionable, so the Warriors could be even thinner at Dallas.
notes.Luguentz Dort: CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings are out, so Atlanta needs more guard and wing minutes. His own minutes had slipped to 18 off the bench Sunday, so the bump depends on the absences rather than his recent trend.
notes.Quentin Grimes: He has started all three games Austin Reaves has missed and played 42 minutes in Tuesday's overtime win, with 21 of his 47 points in the fourth quarter. Reaves was set to test his heel Wednesday morning, and the Lakers have not posted tonight's injury report for this second night of a back-to-back.
notes.Luka Doncic: He played 42 minutes in Tuesday's overtime comeback with Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler both out. Reaves was set to test his heel Wednesday morning and the coach called Kessler's absence precautionary; the Lakers have not posted tonight's report, and this is the second night of a back-to-back against short-handed Utah.
notes.Walker Kessler: He sat Tuesday as a precaution, and the Lakers' coach said the injury is not serious. The Lakers have not posted tonight's injury report; if he sits again, Kevon Looney, Carson Cooper, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jarred Vanderbilt split center minutes as they did Tuesday.
notes.Austin Reaves: He has missed the last two games with a left heel bruise and was set to test it on the court Wednesday morning. The Lakers have not posted tonight's injury report; Quentin Grimes has started in his place.
notes.Brice Sensabaugh: Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are still out, and his bench minutes have climbed in four straight games, to 35 Tuesday. He played the entire fourth quarter and scored 25 of his 40 points in it, but Josh Green is still starting ahead of him, and Utah has not posted tonight's report for this back-to-back.
notes.Keyonte George: He played 35 minutes Tuesday two days after spraining his right ankle, and with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out he and Darryn Peterson carry Utah's offense. Tonight is the second night of a back-to-back, and Utah has not posted its injury report yet.
notes.Mo Bamba: Jusuf Nurkic and Jaxson Hayes are out, and Bamba has started Utah's last two games at center, playing 36 and 31 minutes. Utah has not posted tonight's report for the second night of the back-to-back.
notes.Daniss Jenkins: He has started every Detroit game since 11/9 and played 38 minutes Tuesday. Detroit is thin at guard and wing with Duncan Robinson, Taurean Prince and Ronald Holland II out Tuesday, but tonight is a back-to-back and Detroit has not posted its injury report yet.
notes.Ausar Thompson: Detroit has asked him to run more offense, and he had 12 assists and five steals in Tuesday's win as the team's key defender. He closed the game, but tonight is the second night of a back-to-back and Detroit has not posted its injury report.
notes.Kevin Huerter: He moved into the starting lineup Tuesday with Duncan Robinson out (left quadriceps strain) and played 36 minutes. Detroit has not posted tonight's injury report for the second night of the back-to-back.
notes.Tyrese Maxey: Jaylen Brown is out with a left hamstring strain, which pushes more of Philadelphia's shots to Maxey and Joel Embiid. He has played 35 or 36 minutes in each of his last three games, and Paolo Banchero is out for Orlando.
notes.Joel Embiid: Jaylen Brown is out tonight, and Embiid played 32 minutes Monday on the second night of a back-to-back after sitting Sunday for right plantar fascia management. Philadelphia did not play Tuesday, so he comes in rested.
notes.Bam Adebayo: He sat the second half Monday with right hip tightness but is probable tonight, and Miami said it was being cautious. If he plays a normal night he should be back near the 36 minutes he played on 11/14.
notes.Amen Thompson: He is questionable at Indiana with left knee soreness after missing Monday at Miami. If he sits, Tari Eason likely stays in the starting lineup, and Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun and Fred VanVleet carry more of the offense.
notes.Andrew Nembhard: He is questionable with left hip soreness after missing Sunday's game. With Tyrese Haliburton out, he has played 34 minutes when healthy; if he sits, T.J. McConnell (probable) runs more of the offense.
notes.T.J. McConnell: He is probable with a hamstring strain, and his minutes have risen over his five games since his season debut on 11/7. Tyrese Haliburton is out and Andrew Nembhard is questionable, so he could run the offense for long stretches.
notes.Jarrett Allen: Evan Mobley (toe) is out again, and Allen has started and played 32 and 30 minutes in Cleveland's last two games as the only true big. Memphis is missing Isaiah Stewart, its backup center.
notes.Donovan Mitchell: With Evan Mobley out, he scored 39 against Chicago on Monday in 36 minutes. Peyton Watson (back) is questionable and Jaylon Tyson is doubtful, so Cleveland's wing depth is thin.
notes.Draymond Green: He is questionable at Dallas with right elbow inflammation, an issue he has played through since early November. Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Kristaps Porzingis are all out, so Golden State's offense is very thin.
notes.Cam Spencer: With Ty Jerome out again (right hip) and Scotty Pippen Jr. out week to week, Spencer has started Memphis's last two games and played 34 and 32 minutes.
notes.Zach Edey: He returned Monday and started, playing 21 minutes. Isaiah Stewart (illness) is out again, so there is less competition for center minutes, and Cleveland is without Evan Mobley.
notes.Dean Wade: Jaylen Brown is out tonight, and Wade has played 32 to 35 minutes in each of Philadelphia's last three games, starting two of them.
notes.Kentavious Caldwell-Pope: Jaylen Brown is out tonight, which opens wing minutes; Caldwell-Pope played 31 minutes off the bench Monday after 22 on Sunday.
